title: Jacket potatoes with hake and cavolo nero

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, hake, cavolo nero, garlic, crème fraîche, capers and lemon are all plain foods a grandparent would recognise and keep.

supermarket.reason: Hake fillets, cavolo nero and crème fraîche are all stocked at everyday prices in Tesco and similar shops.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking tray, frying pan and bowl, with simple baking, roasting and frying.

works.reason: An hour at 200°C bakes the potatoes, 12 minutes cooks the hake, and the quantities make a reasonable lunch for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers scrubbing potatoes, shredding greens, slicing garlic, frying and mixing the sauce, and the 60-minute cook matches the bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including lemon zest and juice, chilli flakes and the seasoning, is used, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot jacket potato suits a November lunch, and the cavolo nero is a main topping named in the title rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potato, fish and dark greens make a filling, balanced meal a family would happily eat again.
